## Can health checks be disabled?

Yes, refer to [edit health check](https://docs.byteplus.com/en/docs/clb/Editing-health-check) to turn off the health check switch.

Disabling health checks may affect the normal handling of client access requests. To ensure access requests are not forwarded to abnormal backend servers, it is recommended to enable health checks.

<span id=".5aaC5L2V5aSE55CG5YGl5bq35qOA5p-l5Lqn55Sf55qE5aSn6YeP5pel5b-X77yf"></span>
## How to handle the large volume of logs generated by health checks?

You can adjust the health check "detection interval" or disable health checks, but both carry certain risks. Choose carefully:


1. Detection interval: Extending the health check interval will increase the time CLB takes to detect failures on backend ECS instances.

2. Disabling health checks: The CLB instance no longer checks backend servers. If a backend server fails, traffic cannot automatically switch to other normal backend servers.


We recommend promptly handling the faulty ECS instance.

<span id=".5YGl5bq35qOA5p-l5pSv5oyB55qE5Y2P6K6u57G75Z6L77yf"></span>
## Which protocol types does the health check support?

The CLB instance performs health checks according to the listener protocol (HTTPS listener uses HTTP protocol for health checks). The check port uses the backend server’s business port. The detection principles vary by protocol. For details, refer to the [health check overview](https://docs.byteplus.com/en/docs/clb/Health-check-01).

<span id=".5YGl5bq35qOA5p-l5LuA5LmI5pe25YCZ5ZCv5Yqo77yf"></span>
## When does the health check start?

When a backend server is newly added, the check starts at a random time within the first detection cycle, then follows the configured check interval.

<span id=".5YGl5bq35qOA5p-l5Li65LuA5LmI5Lya5a-86Ie0Q0xC5a6e5L6L6aKR57mB5ZCR5ZCO56uv5pyN5Yqh5Zmo5Y-R6YCB5o6i5rWL6K-35rGC77yf"></span>
## Why does the health check cause the CLB instance to send frequent probe requests to the backend server?

CLB deploys as a high availability cluster. All nodes in the cluster continuously send probe requests to the backend server according to the detection interval. You can control the frequency by adjusting the health check interval.

<span id=".5Li65LuA5LmI5ZCO56uv5pyN5Yqh5Zmo5LiK5pS25Yiw55qE5YGl5bq35qOA5p-l5oql5paH6Ze06ZqU5ZKM6K6-572u55qE6Ze06ZqU5pe26Ze05LiN5LiA6Ie077yf"></span>
## Why is the interval between health check packets received by the server inconsistent with the configured interval?

Each node in the CLB cluster probes the backend server, and the interval of each node matches the configured interval.

The backend server receives multiple probe packets from multiple nodes, so multiple health check packets will be received within the interval period.

<span id=".5paw5Yib5bu655qE55uR5ZCs5Zmo77yM5re75Yqg5ZCO56uv5pyN5Yqh5Zmo5ZCO77yM5Li65LuA5LmI55uR5ZCs5Zmo55qE5YGl5bq35qOA5p-l54q25oCB5LuN5Li64oCc5peg55uu5qCH4oCd77yf"></span>
## Why does the health check status of the listener remain “No target” after creating a new listener and adding backend servers?

The health check cycle for probing backend server status is one minute. After adding backend servers, wait one minute before refreshing the page.

<span id=".5ZCO56uv5pyN5Yqh5Zmo5p2D6YeN6K6-572u5Li6MOWvueWBpeW6t-ajgOafpeacieS7gOS5iOW9seWTje-8nw=="></span>
## How does setting the backend server weight to 0 affect health checks?

CLB does not forward requests to abnormal nodes when health checks fail. Weight is controlled by CLB itself and is unrelated to health checks. Health checks determine whether backend servers are available. Only servers that pass health checks receive forwarded requests. Weight configures the request allocation ratio in scheduling algorithms (such as weighted round robin). These functions operate independently.

<span id=".5LiD5bGC55uR5ZCs5Zmo6L-b6KGM5YGl5bq35qOA5p-l5L2_55So55qE5LuA5LmI5pa55rOV77yf"></span>
## What method does the layer 7 listener use for health checks?

The health checks of layer 7 listeners support GET and HEAD methods.

If health check is enabled on the layer 7 listener, ensure the backend server service does not disable GET or HEAD methods.

<span id=".6LSf6L295Z2H6KGh55uR5ZCs5Zmo5omn6KGM5YGl5bq35qOA5p-l55qESVDlnLDlnYDmmK_ku4DkuYjvvJ8="></span>
## What IP addresses does the CLB listener use to perform health checks?

The CLB listener uses IP addresses from the 100.64.0.0/10 CIDR block to perform health checks.

<span id=".VURQ5Y2P6K6u55uR5ZCs5Zmo55qE5YGl5bq35qOA5p-l54q25oCB5LiN5YeG56Gu5piv5LuA5LmI5Y6f5Zug77yf"></span>
## Why is the health check status of the UDP protocol listener inaccurate?

The UDP protocol listener may show inaccurate health check status, where the health check status does not match the actual state of the backend server port. Possible causes:


* The timeout setting is too short, causing CLB to not receive ICMP messages returned by the backend server within the timeout period and mistakenly consider the health check successful.

   In this case, adjusting the timeout setting of the UDP protocol listener can resolve the issue. For detailed steps on modifying the timeout, refer to [editing UDP protocol health check](https://docs.byteplus.com/en/docs/clb/Editing-health-check).

* The backend server on the Linux system limits the sending rate of ICMP messages to prevent ICMP attacks, causing CLB to not receive the ICMP messages returned by the backend server within the timeout period and mistakenly consider the health check successful.

   In this case, execute the following command on the Linux backend server to cancel the ICMP rate limiting.

   `sysctl -w net.ipv4.icmp_ratemask=6160`


For a detailed explanation of UDP protocol health check principles, see [UDP listener health check principles](https://docs.byteplus.com/en/docs/clb/Health-check-01#6Qww8SqG).
